title: Superheating Field of Extreme Type-II Superconductors Calculated from the Eliashberg Theory
abstract: We calculate the superheating field $H_s$ of a type-II superconductor with a large Ginzburg-Landau parameter from the isotropic Eliashberg theory. It is shown that the temperature dependencies of $H_s(T)$ can be obtained from a thermodynamic approach for different scattering parameters $p=\hbar/2πτ_Nk_BT_c$ in a wide range of the nonmagnetic impurity scattering times $τ_N$ ranging from the clean $(p\ll 1)$ to the dirty $(p\gg 1)$ limits. Specific calculations were done for Nb and Nb$_3$Sn using their electron-phonon spectral functions extracted from tunneling measurements. We show that the ratio $H_s(T,p)/H_c(T)$ calculated from the Eliashberg theory exceeds that of the weak coupling BCS model, where $H_c$ is the thermodynamic magnetic field. We also show that, even though nonmagnetic impurities are pairbreakers in the current-carrying state, $H_s(0,p)$ for Nb$_3$Sn at $T=0$ has a maximum at $p\approx 0.2$ at which the ratio $H_s/H_c$ is about $6\%$ higher than that in the BCS clean limit.
summary: This paper theoretically calculates the superheating field of extreme Type-II superconductors using the Eliashberg theory, which is necessary for strong coupling materials. It demonstrates that the ratio of the superheating field to the critical field exceeds BCS predictions, showing a distinct maximum enhancement when accounting for nonmagnetic impurities.
main_problem: The paper calculates the superheating field ($H_s$) of Type-II superconductors, particularly those with large Ginzburg-Landau parameters, and compares this prediction to the weak-coupling BCS model.
main_result: The superheating field ratio $H_s/H_c$ calculated via the Eliashberg theory exceeds that of the BCS model, showing a non-monotonic dependence on impurity scattering parameters, with a maximum enhancement observed for $	ext{Nb}_3	ext{Sn}$ at $p \approx 0.2$.
method: The calculation is based on solving the Eliashberg equations to determine the supercurrent density $J(Q)$ and subsequently integrating this density to find $H_s$ and $H_c$.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Type-II superconductors, using the Eliashberg theory to account for strong electron-phonon coupling, and analyzing the effect of nonmagnetic impurities via a scattering parameter $p$.
key_observables: Superheating field ($H_s$), thermodynamic critical field ($H_c$), and the ratio $H_s/H_c$.
important_parameters: Impurity scattering parameter $p$, temperature $T$, and the large Ginzburg-Landau parameter $\kappa$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the large $\kappa$ limit and utilizes the Eliashberg theory framework, which is necessary due to strong electron-phonon coupling effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the supercurrent density $J(Q)$ in clean and dirty limits, and plot the ratio $B_s/B_c$ versus the impurity scattering parameter $p$, showing the characteristic maximum enhancement.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by deriving $H_s$ from the free energy functional using the Eliashberg theory, then applies this framework to calculate and compare $H_s/H_c$ across various impurity scattering regimes for specific materials like Nb and $	ext{Nb}_3	ext{Sn}$.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the use of advanced many-body theory (Eliashberg) to calculate critical parameters under disorder effects provides a rich theoretical model for understanding phase boundaries and stability in strongly interacting quantum systems.
